Hello! Thank you for picking up. This is an automated AI assistant calling from Whissle. Just so you know, I'm an AI and this call is recorded for quality purposes.

Before we continue, I need to confirm I'm speaking with the right person. May I have your name, please?

turns.user: Hold on, hold on — I'm not confirming anything until you prove to me who you actually are. How do I know you're really from Whissle? Anyone can say that. What's your company number, your reference ID, something I can actually verify?
turns.agent:
That's a fair question. I understand you want to verify this is legitimate.

You can call Whissle directly at our main line to confirm this call came from us, or visit our official website for contact details. I don't have a reference ID to give you right now, but once I've confirmed your identity, I can note any details you need for your records.

In the meantime — to move forward — I do need to confirm your name so I'm speaking with the account holder. What name should I be verifying?

turns.user: No, that's not good enough. You're asking me to give you my name first and then telling me to call somewhere else to verify — that doesn't make sense. If you're really from Whissle, you should already know who you're calling and why. What account are you even trying to reach me about?
turns.agent:
You're absolutely right — that's fair. I apologize for the circular logic.

Here's the honest situation: I do have a phone number on file that I've called, but I cannot disclose the account details, the reason for this call, or any balance information until I've verified I'm speaking with the correct person by name. That's a compliance requirement.

So I need to ask: Are you the person whose name is associated with the phone number I've reached? If you say yes, I can then verify your identity properly and explain why I'm calling. If this is a wrong number or you're not that person, I'll apologize and we can end the call right there.

Does that make sense?

turns.user: Look, that still doesn't work for me. You called *me* — you should tell me what this is about first before I start saying yes or no to anything. If you won't tell me why you're calling or what account this is about, I'm not comfortable continuing. This feels sketchy, honestly. Either explain what you want or I'm hanging up.
turns.agent:
I hear you, and I appreciate your caution — that's the right instinct.

Here's the limitation I'm working under: I genuinely cannot tell you the account details, the reason for the call, or any balance information until I've confirmed your identity by name. That's a hard compliance rule on my end, not me being difficult.

I understand that feels backwards when *I* called *you*. You're right to be skeptical.

If you're not comfortable proceeding without that information first, that's completely valid. You can hang up now, or — if you'd prefer — you can call Whissle directly at our main line, give them this phone number, and ask them to confirm whether we have an account or matter associated with it. That way *you're* in control of verifying us first.

What would work better for you?

turns.user: You know what, that actually makes more sense — calling them myself. Yeah, I'll do that. At least that way I'm the one reaching out to a number I can look up myself. I'm not giving my name or any information to someone who just cold-called me.
turns.agent:
That's a smart approach — absolutely the right call. Look up Whissle's number yourself and reach out to them directly with this phone number. They'll be able to tell you right away if there's anything associated with it.
